body:
## Summary

- Reuse idle and invalidated building-gradient fields and their search queues in bounded pools (2 MiB per map for fields; 64 searches and 8 MiB for queues).
- Reuse per-thread scratch arrays in Cortex water, wheat, and placement scans, and in Nicowar's defense scan.
- Add a regression for reused building-gradient storage without stale routes.

These are storage changes; no save format, replay format, network version, AI decision rule, or intended game feel changes.

## Measured allocation churn

macOS arm64 optimized headless client, Playground, seed 2287, 8 AI teams (`nicowar,warrush,econo,castor,numbi,cortex,cabino,nicowar`), ticks 5,000–20,000. A malloc/free interposer counted requested bytes by stack; these numbers are allocation volume, not retained memory or time saved.

| Build | Allocation calls | Requested bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Original code (`80aba7aca`) | 1,052,818 | 1,267,534,448 |
| Gradient + Cortex prototype | 816,876 | 215,251,752 |
| Final, including Nicowar and larger search pool | 747,962 | 95,021,336 |

The final run is 92.5% lower in requested bytes and 29.0% lower in allocation calls than the original. With identical headless build flags, the final change from the gradient + Cortex prototype cut another 55.9% of requested bytes. Search-pool slot rejections fell from 1,431 at 16 slots to 33 at 64 slots. A 32-slot trial left 124,194,080 requested bytes, so 64 slots was retained. In one paired run, peak RSS was 76,496,896 bytes at 16 slots and 80,035,840 bytes at 64 slots (+3.5 MB). No speed improvement is claimed.

The same `-test-games-nox 1 --map Playground --matchup nicowar,warrush,econo,castor,numbi,cortex,cabino,nicowar` command was run with `GLOB2_TEST_SEED=2287` and `GLOB2_TEST_MAX_TICKS=5000` or `20000`, with local `artifacts/churn/churn.dylib` interposed and `GLOB2_CHURN_OUT` set to distinct TSV paths. The profiler source, before/after traces, representative saves, commands, and comparison tables are on a dedicated [evidence branch](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/codex/memory-churn-evidence/artifacts/churn); the full local per-tick checksum file is too large for Git and its digest is in `structured-release/checksums.sha256`. This evidence branch is separate from the code PR and will not be merged. On SmallForTwo, seed 1441, Nicowar/Warrush, the final tick window requested 16,552,839 bytes versus 22,517,943 for the earlier gradient-only prototype.

## Verification

- A structured 20,000-tick Playground run with one compute thread, saves every 5,000 ticks and final, and `--telemetry checksums` produced an uncompressed 712,394,624-byte per-tick checksum artifact byte-identical to the pre-change run. SHA-256: `0a7e083697a48a619896cf4b3ac024209b45a56a53fe823bf7b712e9b9c4aa8a`.
- All four checkpoint saves and the final save were byte-identical; final save SHA-256: `b621cbfde880875a4ecd91b95fc2d6c4cb8da1c3f740b6df6bc10e0d54c5ff5b`.
- Loading the pre-change 10,000-tick checkpoint into the changed binary produced the same final save as loading it into the pre-change binary. Both resumed runs differ from the uninterrupted run; that continuity discrepancy predates this patch.
- A four-compute-thread 5,000-tick run produced a byte-identical final save to the pre-change binary.
- `BuildingGradientInvalidationHarness`, `PathGradientHarness` (1,526 cases, digest `3281260807785418242`), `CortexGeometryHarness` (184,704 comparisons), and `run-savegame-safety-tests.py` passed.

Cross-platform checksum comparison remains for CI; local profiling and full-game checks were on macOS arm64. This touches core engine storage and should receive human maintainer approval and a play check before merge per `AGENTS.md`.

comments.body: Bradley confirms Giszmo approved this change in person. I am waiting for the cross-platform checks to finish before merging, as required by AGENTS.md.

Final merge validation for rebased head `822fc1493` (base `60c63032c`): Linux 22.04/24.04 builds and variants, Windows client/server, WebAssembly, browser gateway, and all three Android native builds passed. Six of eight Linux test shards passed. Both shard-1 failures are the `MapRenderResizeHarness.cpp:287` `expected>0` assertion; the same assertion fails in the current master run [36657049347](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36657049347) and the prior master run [36654425222](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36654425222). Ubuntu 24.04 map sweep A failed before checkout because the runner's Microsoft package feed returned HTTP 403 during `apt-get update`; the other map sweeps and telemetry checks passed.

The Linux aggregate therefore cannot pass and CI's browser/native simulation equivalence job is blocked by its dependency chain. Cross-platform per-tick checksums remain unverified. The macOS arm64 before/after 20,000-tick checksum artifact and save comparisons are byte-identical, as documented in the PR body and evidence branch. Bradley confirms Giszmo approved this core engine storage change in person; that approval was recorded earlier in this PR.

title: Reuse gradient and AI scratch storage to reduce memory churn
